transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, um—yeah. I guess what finally scared me into making the appointment is work stuff. I’m a camera operator and editor, and I keep making these dumb technical mistakes that I absolutely know better than to make. Like labeling camera cards wrong, or missing a timecode note, or exporting a client cut with the wrong lower-third—even after I swear I checked it.

And it’s embarrassing, because this is not new to me, you know? I’ve been doing this kind of work long enough that I should not be messing up basic things. It makes me feel like I’m constantly catching fires I started myself.
Do you find yourself feeling anxious or worried about things in general, even when there isn’t a specific problem at work?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, I get worried when there’s an actual thing happening—like if I know I missed something or someone’s waiting on me. But “in general”… I don’t know.

Sometimes I feel keyed up, but then I’ll be like, is that worry or just me having too much coffee and three edit windows open? Sorry, that’s probably not what you asked. I don’t think I’m walking around worrying about random things all the time, if that’s what you mean.
Have you been feeling down, hopeless, or have you lost interest in things you used to enjoy, even outside of work?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in a big, obvious way. I mean, I have days where I’m frustrated or I feel kind of defeated, especially after I’ve messed something up, but I wouldn’t say I’m walking around feeling hopeless.

Interest in things… I don’t know. I still want to do things I like, I just sometimes end up not doing them because I get sidetracked or the day gets away from me. Like I’ll plan to watch a movie or go meet someone, and then suddenly I’m reorganizing hard drives or looking up some totally unrelated thing for two hours. But it’s not that I don’t care about anything anymore, if that makes sense.
Have you noticed that you feel more tired than usual, even if you haven’t been doing anything particularly exhausting?

I don’t know that I’ve noticed that, exactly. I mean, I get tired after long days, sure, especially if I’ve been staring at footage forever—there’s this weird eye-tired thing that happens when you’ve watched the same shot like twenty times and you start questioning reality.

But more tired than usual for no reason? I’m not sure. I haven’t really been tracking it. Some days I feel drained, but then I can usually point to something, like a late edit or just not stopping when I should. So… I guess I wouldn’t say it’s a big thing I’ve noticed.
Do you find it hard to relax, even when you’re not actively working or dealing with a problem?

Yeah… relaxing is kind of weird for me. Like, if there’s downtime, I don’t usually just sit there and do nothing. Even on lighter shoot days, I’ll finish one thing and then immediately start packing gear, or I’ll tweak camera settings that probably don’t need tweaking, or I’ll go into the edit bay and start reorganizing bins.

And then my assistants will be like, “Can you stop for five minutes?” Not in a mean way, more like they’re exhausted just watching me bounce from one thing to the next. I’ll think I’m just being efficient, but I guess it doesn’t look very relaxing from the outside.
Do you ever feel physically restless, like you can't sit still or you're always needing to move around, even when you're not trying to be productive?

Yeah, definitely. Sitting through a client screening is probably the worst example. I know I’m supposed to just sit there and watch quietly like a normal person, but after a while it feels like there’s this pressure building under my skin, like I need to stand up or pace or… I don’t know, do something with my body.

And it’s annoying because it’s not even about being productive at that point. I’m not thinking, “Oh, I should fix that shot,” well—sometimes I am, but even when I’m not, I still feel like I need to move. Like my legs are just waiting for permission.
Do you ever feel physically restless or agitated, like you can’t sit still or need to move around, even when you’re not trying to get something done or feeling anxious about something?

Yeah, I think so. I mean, the clearest thing is client screenings, where I’m supposed to just sit and watch quietly, and everyone’s being professional and still, and I’m there feeling like there’s this pressure building under my skin.

It’s not always that I’m anxious or trying to get something done. Sometimes I know there’s nothing for me to do in that moment, but my body still feels like it wants permission to get up, pace, adjust something, anything. It’s like sitting still becomes its own whole task.

Can you recall if these difficulties with staying still, getting distracted, or feeling like you're always doing something have been a pattern going back to when you were younger, like in school or when you were first starting out in your career?

Yeah, I think it goes way back. Like, even in elementary school, I remember teachers moving my desk around because I was always popping out of my seat or turning around to talk to someone.

And I’d blurt out answers before I even realized I was doing it. Or I’d bug classmates, not trying to be obnoxious exactly, just… I’d already be halfway into saying something or poking at them before my brain caught up. It’s funny, I can still picture this one classroom with those little metal-sided desks—sorry, that’s probably not important. But yeah, it was definitely already there when I was a kid.
